newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end higher, but seen wavering.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end higher, but seen wavering.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed higher Tuesday on short-covering sparked by a powerful rally in U.S. treasuries, dealers said.
But the market could struggle to stay in positive territory Wednesday due to a surge in volume.

"The market reacted to the nosedive today in the U.S. long bond yield, which set the tone for the international markets and forced people who were bearish to cover their bets," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.4 percent to 570.16, while the broad market index advanced 0.9 percent.
Floor volume doubled to 21.7 million pesos in the session, while over-the-counter turnover was virtually unchanged from Monday at 87.8 million pesos.
"It's always tricky when you have such a sudden rise in volume, especially when it comes hand in hand with end-of-month position squaring," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.

The U.S. long bond yield dived to 6.68 percent from 6.84 percent Tuesday on optimism generated by new economic data. Traders warned the markets could see sharp swings if the yield reacts as strongly to other key indicators due this week.

"Between now and the U.S. presidential elections it will be hard to buck the general trend on Wall Street, which means we could rise or fall pretty erratically depending on what the indicators say," said another trader.
The raft of U.S. economic reports continues Wednesday with third-quarter GDP and Friday with October jobs data.
In the bolsa session risers smashed decliners 39 to four and 21 issues closed unchanged.
Best main-tier performers were petrochemical concern Atanor and steelmaker Acindar, which jumped 3.8 percent and 3.7 percent, respectively.

Agricultural holding company Cresud rose 3.0 percent, steelmaker Siderca tacked on 2.9 percent and textile firm and shoemaker Alpargatas closed up 2.7 percent. The only MerVal loser was power utility Capex, which shed 2.0 percent.

Traders said beyond the international factor and the underlying weakness of the bolsa over the past two weeks, blamed partly on a political row over corruption, investors were likely to be cheered by official data showing a 11.1 percent rise in September industrial output. This compares to a 9.2 percent forecast by private consultants FIEL.
